form7-01.note: Opened. Deccan Chronicle, 4 Sept 2026 (IST). Quote is verbatim. The story is datelined Hyderabad and does not say whether the 50,000 figure is statewide or for Hyderabad district; the CEO's own count on 1 October was 28,753 statewide (form7-02), so 'in Telangana' says more than the source. The constituency-level request is supported: a party representative at the meeting chaired by the DEO said they urged Forms 9, 10 and 11 at Assembly constituency level.
form7-01.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported, in a story datelined Hyderabad that does not say whether the figure covers the state or the district, that the Commission had received close to 50,000 Form 7 applications against entries in the draft roll, and that parties at a meeting chaired by Hyderabad's District Election Officer asked for the Form 10 lists by Assembly constituency.

form7-02.note: Opened. Telangana Today, 1 Oct 2026. Figures (28,753 statewide, about 5,000 in Hyderabad) and the 'special care' line are in the source; the paper spells the name Sudharsan. The quote joined two non-adjacent paragraphs without a trim mark; ellipsis added.
form7-02.quote: Revealing SIR of electoral rolls status in the State on Thursday, Telangana Chief Electoral Officer C Sudharsan Reddy said 28,753 Form-7 applications were filed, so far. ... “Special care is being taken while deciding the Form-7 received in bulk. All claims and objections will be placed on the website of the CEO, so that citizens are able to see the list and lodge objections, if any,” he said.

form7-03.note: Opened. Siasat, 1 Oct 2026. Quote verbatim. Siasat says the applications were against a Congress booth agent and about 30 members of his family; it does not give the number of forms, so 'about 30 Form 7 applications' is reworded. The response used a 'rather than' turn; rewritten. Private individuals named in the source (the booth agents) are not named in the claim.
form7-03.claim: Siasat reported that the Telangana Congress complained to the Chief Electoral Officer that a BJP booth agent in Musheerabad had filed Form 7 applications against a Congress booth agent and about 30 members of his family, on forms that were printed in advance. This is the Congress's allegation.
form7-03.response: Siasat reported that the Congress asked for an investigation to establish the facts, including a forensic examination of whether the forms came from a common source.

form7-04.note: Opened. The South First, 2 Oct 2026. Quote verbatim. The in-charges allegation is Pulipati Rajesh Kumar's (Congress), relayed from a BJP insider, and is attributed to the Congress. CEO's press-briefing line is in the article.

form7-05.note: Opened. Deccan Chronicle, 4 Oct 2026. Quote verbatim. Booth 173, the account via Congress sources, the BLO's refusal and the DEO's reported direction to the Musheerabad ERO are all in the article.

form7-06.note: Opened. The News Minute, 4 Oct 2026. Quote verbatim. Owaisi's remarks at the 3 October gathering and the Congress leaders' statement about unsigned forms are in the article.

form7-07.note: Opened. Siasat, 5 Oct 2026, byline Press Trust of India. Quote verbatim. Karnan's statements (not in bulk, Goshamahal unsigned, Musheerabad electors found residing) and Ramchander Rao's denial and the CEO's 1 October remark are in the article.

form7-08.note: Opened. The News Minute, 5 Oct 2026. Quote verbatim and the claim matches the CEO notice as quoted. The response cited a Siasat report saying action would follow an inquiry, which was not found in any source checked; the remark about the CEO website is a research note, not a response. Response cleared.

form7-09.note: Opened. The South First, 5 Oct 2026. Claim supported, including the request to inquire into the BJP state president's role if the allegation is established. The quote joined two non-adjacent paragraphs; ellipsis added.
form7-09.quote: One such form seen by South First had the voter’s name and address pre-filled while the applicant’s details were blank. ... The Congress alleged that the forms had been printed in advance and asked the police to establish whether the persons named as applicants had actually signed them or even knew about the applications.

form7-10.note: Opened. Deccan Chronicle, 6 Oct 2026, from ANI. Quote verbatim. Owaisi said the forms were submitted with a BJP supporter listed as the applicant; he did not say that person brought them. Claim reworded and the private applicant is not named. The response cited an unlocated Siasat report of the same day; replaced with the BJP denial in Siasat/PTI of 5 October (form7-07).
form7-10.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported that Asaduddin Owaisi alleged that pre-printed Form 7s seeking the deletion of 122 electors, all Muslim, were submitted at booth 28 in Goshamahal in the name of a BJP supporter, and that the booth officer refused them. This is AIMIM's allegation.
form7-10.response: Siasat reported on 5 October, citing PTI, that BJP state president N. Ramchander Rao said no BJP booth agents had submitted any such Form 7 applications.

form7-11.note: Opened. Deccan Chronicle, 7 Oct 2026 IST (00:10). Claim supported: ERO complaint on DEO's direction, case at Chikkadpally under BNS 217, 318(2) and RP Act s.31, 30 pre-printed forms, first such instance in Telangana. Quote joined non-adjacent sentences; ellipsis added.
form7-11.quote: The case was booked under BNS Sections 217 (giving false information to a public servant) and 318 (2) (cheating) and Section 31 of the Representation of People Act (making false declarations). ... “The BLO concerned and BLO supervisor collectively refused to receive the bulk forms in spite of repeated requests from the said BLA of BJP and have not given any acknowledgement in token of receipt…,” the FIR copy read.

form7-12.note: Opened. Telangana Today, 6 Oct 2026. Quote verbatim and the claim matches.

form7-13.note: Opened. Deccan Chronicle, 22 June 2026. Quote verbatim. Karnan, DEO, at a press meet.

form7-14.note: Opened. Deccan Chronicle, 7 July 2026. Quote verbatim. Allegation attributed to the BJP; the memorandum also alleges BLOs gave MIM leaders access to the ECI App to upload filled forms.

form7-15.note: Opened. Deccan Chronicle, 29 July 2026. Quote verbatim. Marri Shashidhar Reddy is named as a party office-bearer, which is acceptable.

form7-16.note: Opened. The ADR page is a repost of a Frontline article by Soni Mishra, dated 2 Feb 2026 on ADR's page. The original at Frontline opens and carries the quote verbatim, published 2026-02-02. 29 January is the date of Venugopal's letter, not of the report. Outlet, URL and date corrected to the original. The response cited a News On AIR report of 17 January that was not checked; replaced with the Scroll report (form7-19) that carries the same rule from a Commission official.
form7-16.claim: Frontline reported that Congress general secretary K. C. Venugopal wrote to the Commission on 29 January alleging misuse of Form 7 in several states, and that the Commission said there was no limit on forms per voter but that an ERO must verify when one person files more than five.
form7-16.response: Scroll reported on 23 January 2026 that a senior Commission official in Guwahati gave the same rule.

form7-17.note: Opened. National Herald, 19 Jan 2026 (with PTI inputs). Quote verbatim. Khatra interception, police seizure and inquiry, and the BJP's counter-allegation are in the article.

form7-18.note: Opened. National Herald, 16 Feb 2026. Quote verbatim. The 16 February deadline and statutory disposal instruction are in the article.

form7-19.note: Opened. Scroll, 23 Jan 2026. Claim supported (133 voters, 'half-printed and half-handwritten', Nagaon suspension, the official's rule). The BLO is not named in the claim. The quote joined two non-adjacent passages; ellipsis added.
form7-19.quote: In several Muslim-majority districts and areas of Assam, bulk objections have been filed against voters, seeking to strike their names off the electoral roll. ... In Nagaon district, the hearing process has been suspended in three Assembly constituencies after complaints of fake Form 7 applications.

form7-20.note: Opened. Scroll, 24 Jan 2026. Quote verbatim. Tasa's response is in the article. No private person named in the claim.

form7-21.note: Opened Scroll's rewrite and the original it links, The Indian Express, published 28 Jan 2026, where Sarma speaks to reporters on Tuesday. Corrected to the original. The original quote also has him say he told BJP people to keep giving complaints against 'Miyas'; the claim now reports that as his words.
form7-21.claim: The Indian Express reported that Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma told reporters he had told BJP members to keep filing complaints against people he called 'Miyas' and to fill Form 7s wherever possible during the Special Revision.
form7-21.quote: I myself have told the BJP people that they should keep giving complaints against Miyas. There is nothing to hide about this. I have held meetings, I have done video conferences, and I have told people that, wherever possible, they should fill Form 7s.

form7-22.note: Opened. Scroll, 11 Feb 2026, citing PTI. Quote verbatim. No PTI original URL was found; kept as the Scroll copy.

form7-23.note: Opened. Scroll, 19 Jan 2026. Claim supported; Dak's response is in the article. The quote joined non-adjacent sentences; ellipsis added.
form7-23.quote: “In every Assembly constituency, 10 thousand to 15 thousand fake computerised forms are printed,” he claimed. ... He added that several booth-level agents had given statements to the media that they had not signed these forms, and that the signatures were forged and the applications were incomplete.

form7-24.note: Opened. The Quint, 12 Feb 2026. Claim supported: forms filed in BJP BLAs' names, BLAs saying signatures were forged, no FIR or inquiry nearly a month on, calls to DM and SDM unanswered. The quote joined two non-adjacent paragraphs; ellipsis added.
form7-24.quote: As per copies of forms, seen by The Quint, they were overwhelmingly filed under the names of Booth Level Agents (BLAs) working for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and predominantly targeted Muslim voters in Rural Alwar. ... Yet no FIR, no administrative inquiry, no forensic audit of handwriting or digital origin has been announced in Alwar.

form7-25.note: Opened. Newslaundry, 11 Feb 2026. Newslaundry says 269 objectors filed the 15,000-odd applications, each 50 or more, and that 'a staggering number' appeared pre-filled; it does not say all were printed. Claim reworded. The quote joined non-adjacent sentences; ellipsis added. DEO Upadhyay's response is in the article.
form7-25.claim: Newslaundry reported that the 15,663 Form 7s in Somnath were filed by 269 people, each filing 50 or more, that copies it reviewed had the voter's details printed in English and the objector's details handwritten in Gujarati, and that six of the objectors filed affidavits saying they had not filed them.
form7-25.quote: Of the 15,663 Form-7 applications, a staggering number appeared to be pre-filled and then submitted by just 269 people. ... Newslaundry has reviewed copies of Form-7s where voter details – such as name, mobile number, constituency, EPIC number, and booth number – are printed in English, while the objectors' details are handwritten in Gujarati.

form7-26.note: Opened. Deccan Herald, 9 May 2026. Quote verbatim. Notice issued Friday, next hearing 7 July. Petitions from Kodinar and Sidhpur.

form7-27.note: Opened. ETV Bharat, 30 Jan 2026. Quote verbatim. The objector who denied filing is not named in the claim. DEO's response is in the article.

form7-28.note: Opened. Siasat, 20 Mar 2026, citing The Indian Express; no link to the original was given and it could not be opened from here, so kept as the Siasat copy. Quote verbatim. The printing is 'allegedly' in the source; claim now says so.
form7-28.claim: Siasat reported, citing The Indian Express, that Form 7s against 544 voters of a Shamli village were found with a booth officer, said to have been already printed with the voters' EPIC numbers, and that the District Magistrate said the forms were fake and the probe found nothing.

form7-29.note: Opened. The Pioneer, 22 Aug 2026. Quote verbatim; figures attributed to Congress's Manoj Rawat. CEO and Additional CEO responses are in the article. Grammar fix only ('an Uttarakhand').
form7-29.claim: The Pioneer reported that an Uttarakhand Congress delegation told the Chief Electoral Officer that one person had filed objections against about 6,400 voters and about 1,200 people had filed more than ten each. These are the Congress's figures.

form7-30.note: Opened. Newslaundry, 28 Aug 2026. Quote verbatim; 35 affidavits, 1,657 objections, 31 BJP BLA-2s. The ERO said the objections were cancelled because those named had sought to withdraw them. ERO referred to by office.
form7-30.response: Newslaundry quoted the Jhabrera ERO saying the objections were cancelled after those named sought to withdraw them and the voters would not be deleted, and that the Election Commission would not order any investigation and those whose names were misused should file an FIR.

form7-31.note: Opened The Wire's rewrite and the original it links, The Hindu, published 29 Sept 2026 (23:45 IST). Form 10 reports for 21 to 27 September, four individuals over 10 a day, no limit on ECINET: all in the original. Corrected to the original. The Hindu reports the Delhi CEO's office did not respond.
form7-31.claim: The Hindu reported that Form 10 lists published for 21 to 27 September showed four people in Delhi filing more than ten applications a day through the Commission's ECINET portal, which does not enforce the limit of ten a day for booth agents.
form7-31.quote: Fresh lapses have come to light in the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) exercise in Delhi, with official data showing that booth-level agents (BLAs) bypassed the Election Commission’s (EC) cap on submitting only 10 applications a day during the claims and objections phase by filing through the panel’s ECINET portal, which has no such restriction in place. ... The software has no mechanism to impose the prescribed limit, effectively allowing the guidelines to be bypassed.
form7-31.response: The Hindu reported that the office of Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer did not respond to a request for comment.

form7-32.note: Opened. The News Minute, 3 Oct 2026. It combines two The Hindu reports (Belagavi, 1 Oct; legal tenability of FIRs, 1 Oct) with the CEO's press release, so it is kept as the source. Claim and response supported. The quote joined non-adjacent paragraphs; ellipsis added.
form7-32.quote: The names and other details of voters had already been filled in, while the names of the persons shown as objectors were either handwritten or left blank. ... None of the five FIRs filed in connection with the Karnataka cases invokes the Representation of the People Act.

form7-33.note: Opened. The News Minute, 4 Oct 2026 (meeting on 3 October). Quote verbatim; claim supported. The response used an 'X, not Y' turn; rewritten.
form7-33.response: The News Minute reported that Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara said ministers had gone to the CEO's office to submit a memorandum.

form7-34.note: Opened. Deccan Chronicle, 5 July 2025 IST (the Commission spoke on Friday 4 July). Quote verbatim. Forms distributed on the BLOs' first visit.

form7-35.note: Opened. LiveLaw, 26 July 2025. Quote verbatim. Rejoinder filed in reply to the Commission's counter-affidavit.

form7-36.note: Haldwani Express News page fetched; published 8 Oct 2026, headline matches. The order was issued 6 October 2026 by the JMFC, Haldwani, directing Banbhoolpura police to register an FIR and investigate. The complainant is a BLA-2 who says Form 7s for 28 voters of part 134 were filed online on 12 August in his name and that he neither filed nor authorised them; the court held that identifying who filed them needs police investigation. Police report and the court's reply match the response. Both Hindi fragments verbatim. The complainant is named in the source and not in the item. City News Uttarakhand (8 Oct) carries the same date and part number.

form7-37.note: The Wire page fetched; published 2 Oct 2026 16:23, citing Hindustan Times; CEO data released Thursday 1 October. Headline matches. Quote verbatim. 13,443, 4,790 for Chatra (about 36%), West Singhbhum 1,906 and Deoghar 1,099 all in the report. Response matches the CEO's quoted statement on cross-checking and automatic Form 7 entries from Form 8.

form7-38.note: The News Minute page fetched; published 6 Oct 2026 about the CEO's press conference of 5 October; headline matches. Quote verbatim. 91,278 received 16 June to 4 October, no deletion so far, notice and hearing before an ERO decides, EROs to act on bulk applications after inquiry, and no FIR registered by his office are all in the report. ETV Bharat (5 Oct) agrees.

form7-39.note: ThePrint (PTI, 6 Oct 2026 1:45 pm) opened in full. 'false and unwarranted' verbatim, quoted here in its full sentence. Delegation, Governor, the 'succumbed' allegation and the 5 October meeting with CEO V Anbukkumar are on the page. Not on the site before.

form7-40.note: Punjab Kesari English (IANS, Bengaluru Oct 7, published 7 Oct 2026 22:05) opened in full. Quote verbatim. Ramamurthy is an MLA and BJP district president. The FIR is form7-42.

form7-41.note: Same page as form7-40, opened in full. Quote verbatim. The page says 'Shanivarasante Police Station in Madikeri district' and the 64 voters in Byadagutta village. The complainant and the five accused are named on the page and are given by role here.

form7-42.claim: Jayanagar police in Bengaluru registered an FIR against two BJP booth level agents and others on a complaint by Karnataka Mahila Congress president Sowmya Reddy, The Daily Jagran reported, carrying ANI. The complaint alleged Form 7 applications with forged signatures seeking to delete 5,698 voters by falsely claiming they had shifted.
form7-42.note: The Daily Jagran (6 Oct 2026 16:01 IST) opened in full. Quote verbatim. The story is credited to ANI and the page says it was not edited except the headline, so the outlet carries ANI. FIR registered Monday night, 5 October. Sowmya Reddy is a party office-holder.

form7-43.claim: Chief Minister D K Shivakumar alleged on 6 October that BJP and JD(S) workers had filed Form 7 applications in bulk and then collected back and destroyed more than a lakh of them, threatening booth officers, The News Minute reported. This is his allegation.
form7-43.response: BJP MLC C T Ravi asked the Commission to register a case against people making baseless allegations and sought legal action against Shivakumar.
form7-43.note: The News Minute (7 Oct 2026) opened in full. Quote verbatim, from Shivakumar on Tuesday 6 October. He alleged the forms were collected back and destroyed, and the claim now says so and that it is his allegation. The CEO's statement that no voter had yet been deleted on a Form 7 is the article's paraphrase and is already on the site as form7-38, so it is left out of this item.

form7-44.note: Free Press Journal (4 Oct 2026 20:09 IST) opened in full. Quote verbatim. The letter of 1 October was shared on X. Koppa was not on the site before.

form7-45.claim: Delhi Chief Electoral Officer Ashok Kumar announced on 9 October that the Commission had decided to limit an individual voter to ten Form 7 objections for the whole claims and objections period and five a month during continuous updation, citing bulk objections on unsubstantiated grounds, IANS reported. The statement said registration officers would act against false objections under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
form7-45.note: Social News XYZ (IANS, New Delhi Oct 9) opened in full. Quote verbatim. The statement says the Commission decided the limits, announced by Delhi CEO Ashok Kumar on Friday 9 October, so the claim does not present it as the CEO's own cap. The response is left empty because the item is itself the Commission's decision.

form7-46.note: Merged from two second readings of 2026-10-10. The Wire (7 Oct 2026 16:20 IST) opened in full: quote verbatim, and the 2.12 lakh Form 6 and 51,747 Form 7 were submitted between 16 June and 31 August, before the claims period, which the claim now says. Madhyamam Online (7 Oct 2026 5:13 PM IST) opened: quote and figures verbatim, and 'about six' is The Hindu's own ratio.

form7-47.quote: Election authorities in Telangana on Thursday said 24,323 Form-7 applications have been received so far during SIR of electoral rolls, of which 12,204 names were removed.
form7-47.claim: Data released by Telangana's Chief Electoral Officer on 8 October showed 24,323 Form 7 applications received from 15 June to 7 October and 12,204 names removed, PTI reported. The figure is lower than the 28,753 Form 7s the CEO said on 1 October had been filed, and the reports do not explain the difference.
form7-47.note: ETV Bharat (PTI, 9 Oct 2026 8:58 IST) opened in full. The verbatim sentence is found and added. The data were released on Thursday 8 October and run to 7 October, so the event date is 8 October. Figures confirmed on the page. The conflict with 28,753 (form7-02, Telangana Today of 1 October) cannot be resolved from the sources, so both stay, each with its date and source.

form7-48.claim: The Karnataka High Court stayed proceedings in two FIRs against two BJP booth agents accused over bulk Form 7s against voters in Bengaluru's Malleshwaram constituency, Bar and Bench reported. The judge said the FIRs looked premature because the registration officer had not yet decided the Form 7s.
form7-48.note: Bar and Bench (Siddesh M S, 9 Oct 2026 2:54 pm) opened. The Court stayed the proceedings, not the FIRs as such. Quote verbatim. Ward and voter counts verified. The State's and the complainant's positions are correctly attributed (Additional SPP Anoop Kumar, complainant's advocate Shatabish Shivanna).

form7-49.claim: The Karnataka High Court at Dharwad told the police to take no coercive steps until 13 October against a BJP functionary and two supporters booked over Form 7s against voters in Belagavi, LiveLaw reported. A Congress block agent's complaint, as the police record it, alleges they handed about 198 fabricated Form 7s to the booth officer.
form7-49.quote: Till then, the respondent-police/IO shall not take any coercive steps against the petitioners…
form7-49.note: LiveLaw (8 Oct 2026 9:28 PM IST) opened. The allegation is the complainant's: LiveLaw says 'According to the police, a block agent of the opposing Congress party had alleged' about 198 fabricated Form 7s, so the claim attributes it to the complainant as recorded by police. The quote on the page ends with an ellipsis inside the order extract.
